paper.title: Large Language Model Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers
paper.central_claim: Self-evolving LLM agents depend on raw experience but often disregard or misinterpret condensed experience, even when it is the only experience provided, across single/multi-agent configurations and scales.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; null by design (no probing).

rationale: Format-preserving content interventions on retained raw/condensed experience across four frameworks; strong controlled design with null conclusions resting on single runs, no CIs, unmatched intervention size and success-only proxy. claim_support scoped.

missing_sections: numeric values inside Figures 2-6, 8-19 (figure-embedded; not in extracted text)

evidence.quote: we comprehensively evaluate four representative frameworks across 13 LLM backbones and 9 environments
evidence.support_explanation: Claimed coverage: 4 frameworks (ExpeL, Dynamic Cheatsheet, ReasoningBank, G-Memory), 13 backbones, 9 benchmarks.

evidence.quote: while agents consistently depend on raw experience, they often disregard or misinterpret condensed experience, even when it is the only experience provided
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim (raw vs condensed asymmetry).

evidence.quote: prior work has focused mainly on how such experiences are stored or represented, leaving it unclear whether agents actually and faithfully leverage them to improve performance
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: storage/representation studied, use of experience not tested.

evidence.quote: little attention has been paid to whether agents faithfully rely on the retrieved experiences
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated novelty over experience-driven agent literature.

evidence.quote: Early studies on faithfulness focus on in-context learning of LMs
evidence.support_explanation: Lineage: ICL and CoT faithfulness; nearest agent-memory perturbation studies are not discussed.

evidence.quote: We define experience faithfulness as the extent to which an agent’s behavior is causally grounded in its input experience
evidence.support_explanation: Operational definition: behaviour change under perturbation.

evidence.quote: This is distinct from a full ablation (w/o cond), which omits the condensed experience entirely.
evidence.support_explanation: Empty keeps format cues, w/o removes the block: separates presence/format from content.

evidence.quote: Replace the entire content of condensed experience with semantically empty placeholder tokens
evidence.support_explanation: Filler: format-preserving null for condensed experience.

evidence.quote: Our experiments span 10 LLMs, including closed-source models
evidence.support_explanation: Internal inconsistency with abstract (13 backbones); the listed Qwen3 variants may account for the difference.

evidence.quote: Across both frameworks and nearly all tasks, perturbations such as Corrupt, Irrelevant, and Filler yield performance that is nearly indistinguishable from the unperturbed baseline.
evidence.support_explanation: Main joint-access finding for condensed experience (numbers are inside Figs.2-3, not in extracted text).

evidence.quote: removing raw experience (w/o Raw Exp.) reliably causes substantial performance degradation on most tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Raw experience contributes to retained-store performance.

evidence.quote: removing condensed experience (w/o Condensed Exp.) leads to consistent performance drops across all four WebArena tasks
evidence.support_explanation: In condensed-only ReasoningBank the block helps, yet semantics seem not to matter.

evidence.quote: interventions such as Corrupt, Irrelevant, and even Filler lead to only negligible degradation or even slight improvements
evidence.support_explanation: Null-effect inference from performance; magnitude/uncertainty values are in Fig.4 (not in text).

evidence.quote: performance gains may stem from superficial features, such as the presence of a text block or stylistic patterns (Empty), rather than genuine semantic grounding
evidence.support_explanation: Authors state a hypothesis for presence/format effects; not directly tested beyond Empty/Filler.

evidence.quote: despite substantial performance improvements with scaling, both small and large models remain consistently insensitive to condensed experience interventions
evidence.support_explanation: Scale holds for ExpeL with six Qwen3 variants (Fig.6).

evidence.quote: We observe that in certain knowledge-intensive tasks such as GPQA-Diamond and MMLU-Pro Eng., the agent exhibits comparable sensitivity to both raw and condensed experience.
evidence.support_explanation: Boundary of the asymmetry claim.

evidence.quote: we analyze cases where the agent succeeds without condensed experience but fails when it is added
evidence.support_explanation: Cause analysis conditions on discordant cases; Table 1 gives percentages without counts.

evidence.quote: we use the gradient magnitude of token embeddings as a surrogate for the attention-level IG score
evidence.support_explanation: IG analysis uses an approximation; segment attribution is not a behavioural measure.

evidence.quote: Each benchmark contributes 100 sampled examples, and we report exact match as the evaluation metric.
evidence.support_explanation: Sample size for the prior-knowledge test.

evidence.quote: interventions on raw experience do not significantly hurt performance—sometimes even yielding higher scores
evidence.support_explanation: In multi-hop QA neither form is used; supports the pretrained-prior cause.

evidence.quote: in Musique, several perturbed conditions (e.g., Corrupt or Filler) even outperform ExpeL
evidence.support_explanation: Shows run-to-run/score noise of several points at n=100 is read as no effect, with no CI or test.

evidence.quote: the LLM decoding temperature is set to 0.0, and greedy decoding is used
evidence.support_explanation: Deterministic decoding for ExpeL; single run per cell is implied.

evidence.quote: We selected 100 questions from the distractor dev split following ExpeL for our experiments.
evidence.support_explanation: Benchmarks use 100-task subsets.

evidence.support_explanation: Design takeaway offered without any tested remedy.

gap.author_gap: Experience-driven self-evolving agents are assumed to improve because they use stored experience; work studied how experiences are stored/represented but not whether behaviour causally depends on them.
gap.checked_gap: Real and specific: gains of memory agents could come from format, presence or priors rather than content. Lineage to ICL/CoT faithfulness is clear. The paper does not compare with earlier agent-memory ablation/perturbation studies (e.g., component ablations in the audited frameworks themselves are cited only as frameworks), so the "first" claim is author-stated.
gap.lineage/closest_adjacent: ExpeL / Dynamic Cheatsheet / ReasoningBank / G-Memory (audited systems); ICL-label/demonstration sensitivity studies (Min 2022, Ye & Durrett 2022, Shi 2024); CoT faithfulness (Lanham 2023, Turpin 2023).
gap.residue: No evidence which part of the gains of a retained memory is attributable to its semantic content, by experience form.
gap.stakes: Self-evolving claims and condensation designs may be credited with gains from format or priors.
gap.method_response: Format-preserving content interventions on raw vs condensed experience, condensed-only and multi-agent replications, scale sweep, and three cause analyses.
gap.remaining_gap: Causes remain partly correlational (case counts, IG surrogate); no tested remedy; success-rate proxy; no multi-seed intervals.
gap.unresolved: Earlier agent-memory perturbation/ablation work (neighbours) not pinned in the materials; "first systematic" is not verified.

claims.text: Agents depend on raw experience but largely not on the semantics of condensed experience (joint access).
claims.setting: ExpeL (GPT-4o, 3 benchmarks; replicates Qwen3-235B, Claude-Sonnet-4.6), Dynamic Cheatsheet (GPT-4o)
claims.result/denominator: numbers in Figs.2-3 (not in text); 100-task subsets
claims.allowed_conclusion: In these frameworks and tasks, content-level perturbations of condensed text change success little compared with raw trajectories.

claims.text: Condensed-only: unfaithfulness persists without raw overshadowing.
claims.result/denominator: w/o condensed lowers all four WebArena tasks; semantic perturbations negligible
claims.allowed_conclusion: Block presence helps; semantics not shown to be needed for ReasoningBank.

claims.text: Multi-agent: raw experience from both sources is faithfully used; condensed remains fragile.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Pattern replicates for G-Memory on ALFWorld.

claims.text: Causes: semantically limited condensed content, internal processing biases, and prior-sufficient tasks.

claims.result/denominator: percentages without counts; IG surrogate; n=100 QA

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Content-perturbation and w/o ablations on retained experience stores show how the stores affect later task performance; the construction/test split is inherited from the official frameworks and not described, so level is held at retained without claiming independent held-out evidence. No improver claim.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: For the four audited frameworks, perturbing condensed experience (Corrupt/Irrelevant/Filler) typically leaves task success close to unperturbed while perturbing raw trajectories often lowers it, with exceptions on knowledge-intensive tasks. Author-reported, not our reproduction.
assessment.unresolved: Figure-embedded effect sizes unseen; intervention-size matching; uncertainty; whether success invariance implies unused text.

retention_trace.note: Diagnostic of retained experience stores: before=no or unperturbed experience; change=content interventions on retrieved raw/condensed entries; selection=none; persistence=experience store of each framework; later tasks=benchmark tasks; measured effect=success change.

G.reason: Concrete and important gap (gains of memory agents may not stem from experience semantics) with clear lineage to ICL/CoT faithfulness; nearest agent-memory perturbation/ablation work is not compared or pinned and "first" is author-stated.

M.reason: Format-preserving interventions, condensed-only and multi-agent replications and a prior-knowledge test give distinguishable predictions for presence/format vs semantics; remedy untested and causes partly correlational.

X.reason: Interventions, frameworks, benchmarks, sample sizes and hyper-parameters are specified with examples (Table 3) and code; boundaries (task regime) stated; inconsistencies (10 vs 13 LLMs, temperature 0.7 vs greedy) and unstated build/test split remain.

E.measurement.reason: Task-success metrics are standard and format-preserving nulls exist, but faithfulness is operationalised as success change without an action-level behaviour measure, and the IG analysis uses an embedding-gradient surrogate.

E.causality.reason: Direct content cuts on the retained store with w/o, Empty, Filler and Corrupt controls plus condensed-only replication make the main asymmetry causal; intervention magnitude differs between raw and condensed and the three causes rely on correlational evidence.

E.holdout.reason: Four frameworks, offline/online and multi-agent settings, many backbones and 9 benchmarks support the scoped claim; the claim of a fundamental property of current designs exceeds four frameworks, backbone-framework matrix is partial and the experience-build/test split is not described.

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes are stated (100-task subsets, WebArena subsets, 134 ALFWorld) but the text and tables (Tables 2 and 7) report single values with no seeds, intervals or tests, while no-change conclusions rest on differences of a few points; figure-internal error bars were not visible in the extracted text.

E.cost.reason: Interaction-step budgets follow each framework and are identical across interventions (matched by construction, so no budget asymmetry), but no token, API or GPU-hour cost is reported.
